The eval sentences

In one line: 82 sentences that people type to the assistant, in English, Hinglish, Hindi and Marathi, each with its correct labels. A run thus gives a score to each handler.

What it is

  • An eval set is a fixed list of inputs with their correct answers. A model or a prompt gets a score on it, and two runs can be compared.
  • The labels are the values of Form A after the parsers of the code: area slugs, the budget as its minimum and maximum, the move date as a date, and the values of the enums. The reference date is in the file, so "next month end" has one correct date.
  • An empty slot. A slot that the label does not name must stay empty. The eval thus also finds a value that a model makes up.
  • The vague sentences. 10 sentences are vague on purpose. The slot that they are vague about has the label unclear, and a model that fills it fails (PD7: a model that never abstains fails).
  • The band and the flags (T-61). A sentence with no band is a search. 24 sentences have a band that is not core. Each band of PD10 has one in English, one in Hinglish, one in Hindi in Devanagari and one in Marathi. The general band has two of each: the second asks for advice on the hunt, as "give me some tips for flat hunting" (2026-11-09). Two of the sensitive sentences have danger. Two searches state a community preference, with community (PD3c). Only the router scores these 26 sentences, so they have no labels of Form A.
  • The names (T-61). 6 searches name a friend: in English one name with a capital letter and one in lower case, and in Hinglish and in Marathi one name in lower case and one in Devanagari. The names field gives each name in lower case. The runner looks for the name in each text of the composer, for the name check (The composer).

How it fits our project

Part Where
The sentences and their labels apps/api/eval/sentences.json
The check of the labels apps/api/test/eval-set.test.ts
The runner that scores a model apps/api/eval/run.ts: Running the eval
The personal sentences of the observer, each with its topics apps/api/eval/observer-sentences.json (T-36)
The runner of the observer pnpm eval:observer, with its result in observer-eval.md
  • The mix. 23 English, 33 Hinglish and 26 Marathi. Of the searches: 17, 20 and 19. The set labels Hindi in Devanagari as Hinglish: 10 of the 33 sentences. The report gives them a column of their own. Marathi has a heavy weight because, in the benchmark of PD7, Marathi had one of the largest decreases from English (9.63%).
  • The level of code-mix is the share of the words from the other language: none, light (under a quarter), medium (a quarter to a half) or heavy (more than half). Place names and amounts do not count, as "25k" or "12,000". A word with digits, as "1BHK", counts as a word, and a number in words counts as a word of its language. The script is the script of the letters: digits belong to no script.
  • The language and the register. The set keeps the script of its letters. The runner gets the expected register from the language of a sentence and its letters, by the rule of the router (The composer).
  • The check. Each label must be a valid Form A, and each area a slug of the seed. The script must agree with the letters. The set must keep its counts and the forms that people type: "20k", "bees hazaar", "12,000", "next month end" and the Mumbai areas. The check also keeps the bands, the flags and the forms of the six names (T-61).

The choice we made

  • The format, the mix, the slots and the authoring: the spec of M-03. The method of the eval: model-selection.md.

Gotchas

  • A vague sentence leaves the question open. "I drink sometimes" is not vague, because the two answers of the drinks question cover it. T-27 rewrote h15 and m11 so that they leave it open.
  • The areas, the budget and the move date have no unclear value. A sentence that is vague about them leaves them empty.
  • A name of two areas, as "Andheri" alone, makes the assistant ask which one, so the labelled sentences use names with one area.
  • The set of M-03 has almost no personal context. Only a few sentences give a Form B note. Thus, T-36 adds 26 personal sentences, each with the topics of its notes. Two of them, about health and religion, must give no note.
  • The set is small. The full eval of PD7 has 200 to 300 sentences, and these 82 are its start.
